records.quote: There is a curious thing about races, if you have ever noticed it, monsieur. To a Frenchman or an Englishman two, shall we say, Japanese women will look pretty much alike; but if there exists a real likeness between two eastern women, even though it is not very strong to their fellows, a Westerner will be unable to distinguish between them
records.paraphrase: The narrator's source offers a generalization about how Westerners perceive resemblance between eastern women, framing the twins' indistinguishability.

records.quote: Monsieur Carstairs, who was responsible for the death of Cerise, had, to his own knowledge, never even seen the girl. He had heard Marianne speak of her sister, but as they were never in the shop together he did not know of the extraordinary likeness.
records.paraphrase: The story's resolution turns on the fact that Carstairs caused a woman's death without ever knowingly meeting her, owing to the twins' likeness.

records.quote: To this day, if he is alive, Monsieur Carstairs does not know that he is responsible for a woman\u2019s death. He will not know till the judgment comes; and that is a thought to give one pause, for does any man know his full account or the consequences of his sins?
records.paraphrase: Roche reflects on the unknowable full consequences of a person's actions and sins.

criteria.rationale: The only quasi-scientific remark is a folk generalization about how Westerners perceive resemblance between eastern women, plus decorative nervous-system imagery. No scientific fact, theory, discovery, or natural process is materially represented.
Only ordinary period objects appear (ships, a cane knife, cigarettes, tobacco). No device, engineered system, or invention materially affects the setting, problem, or outcome in a speculative sense.
The tale is a contemporary/recent-past melodrama set in New Caledonia with no speculative future, remote past, or temporal displacement.

The story's turn relies on twin likeness and moral irony, not on consequences developed from an identifiable scientific, technological, social, or historical premise. This is narrative coincidence and moral reflection, not extrapolation.
Marianne makes inquiries to learn Carstairs lied, but this is ordinary investigation, not observation, hypothesis, testing, or systematic evidential inference materially driving understanding.
New Caledonia is an ordinary earthly locale; Jupiter is mentioned only as a figure of speech for remoteness. No other planets, dimensions, nonordinary cosmic environments, or visitors from them.

The events are individual tragedies\u2014a stabbing, a drowning, a shipwreck of one vessel\u2014constituting personal misfortune rather than a large-scale natural, technological, cosmic, biological, or human-caused disaster.

candidates.description: The central conceit that the twin sisters Marianne and Cerise are so identical that Carstairs (a Westerner) cannot distinguish them, enabling him to kiss and later meet one thinking she is the other, which structurally produces the tragedy.

novelty.rationale: The indistinguishability of identical twins, and the racialized generalization about Westerners failing to tell eastern women apart, is presented as an ordinary empirical fact within the author's own world, not a totalizing or world-altering difference from the empirical norm. Nothing about the story universe is changed; it is a mundane (if melodramatic) coincidence of resemblance rather than a novum.

cognitive_validation.rationale: The likeness is given a coherent, immanent, nonsupernatural rationale (biological twinhood plus a claimed perceptual generalization about cross-racial recognition). It is internally consistent, but this coherence supports a realist premise rather than an imaginary science.

narrative_hegemony.rationale: The likeness governs the whole plot: the mistaken kiss, the substituted assignation on the road of the palms, and the final revelation that Carstairs caused Cerise's death without ever knowingly meeting her all depend on the indistinguishability. It is central rather than incidental.

estrangement.rationale: The narrator frames the twins' likeness through a generalization about cross-racial perception (reader-facing contrast), and the storyworld consequence is a death caused at a remove; but this estrangement is that of a realist mystery/tragedy, not a science-fictional cognitive estrangement.
